model_risks.risk: Shared User has an FK into a tenant table. users.User.home_facility points to facility.Facility. In django-tenants a public table cannot reference a table in a tenant schema, so this blocks migrations. The field is per-hospital anyway: a doctor at two hospitals has two home facilities.
model_risks.evidence: care/users/models.py:142-144. grep finds no use of home_facility outside the model and migrations, so dropping it, or moving it to a tenant-side staff profile, is a small logged CARE edit.

model_risks.risk: Shared User has an FK into emr.Organization (User.geo_organization). If Organization is per tenant, this is another public-to-tenant FK, which is a blocker.

emr.Organization mixes global reference data ('govt' India geography) with hospital-specific data ('team', 'role', 'product_supplier') in one self-referencing tree table. Sharing it leaks other hospitals' teams and role-orgs and puts all tenants' names into one uniqueness check. Making it per tenant duplicates the LGD geography in every schema; at full village level, hundreds of tenants times about 250k villages is large. Splitting it needs either a CARE model change or a geography-only shared table.

User.cached_role_orgs is stored once per person on the shared User row, but it is built from OrganizationUser in whatever tenant schema is active. A doctor at hospitals A and B gets A's role-orgs cached and served in B (stale, and a cross-tenant leak). Cache resets in one tenant overwrite the other.

Redis cache keys are built from integer PKs with no tenant prefix. Each schema has its own sequences, so facility id=1, role id=5 and so on exist in every tenant. Cached facility flags, role permissions and model_from_cache serialisations then leak between tenants. The CACHES setting has no KEY_FUNCTION or KEY_PREFIX. A tenant-aware key function is needed (e.g. django_tenants.cache.make_key), and other raw redis/cache uses need an audit.

With User shared, the user list and search endpoint returns every non-deleted user on the platform. Each hospital would see, and could search, staff from all other hospitals (a DPDP privacy issue). The queryset must be filtered to users who are members of the current tenant.
model_risks.evidence: care/emr/api/viewsets/user.py:103-106 (search_fields first_name/last_name/username; get_queryset filters only deleted=False)

model_risks.risk: is_superuser is a global flag on the shared User and bypasses every authorization check. A CARE superuser would be superuser in every tenant. Platform operators need tenant-scoped admin rights, with superuser reserved for the platform.

Roles need a scope decision. RoleModel holds both code-defined system roles and admin-created custom roles, with a name unique across the whole table. If shared, custom roles leak and collide across hospitals. If per tenant, sync_permissions_roles must run in every schema (and at tenant creation), and Facility.save's get_or_create by role name runs in the tenant schema.

Mixing shared and tenant tables makes hard deletes fail. sync_permissions_roles uses queryset .delete() on PermissionModel, RoleModel and RolePermission. If these sit in public while tenant tables FK into them (OrganizationUser.role CASCADE, PatientUser.role PROTECT), Django's ORM cascade only sees the current search_path. Rows in other schemas are not collected, so the deferred DB FK constraints fail at commit or the sync aborts.

Per-hospital professional data lives on the global User row: user_type, weekly_working_hours, preferences, plus prefix/qualification, which are arguably global. A doctor at two hospitals cannot have different user_type or working hours. A tenant-side staff profile model is needed.

Process-level class caches are not tenant-aware. PatientIdentifierConfigCache keeps mutable class dicts that persist across requests for different tenants in the same worker, with invalidation limited to that process. instance_configs semantics ('facility IS NULL' meaning deployment-wide) now mean tenant-wide.

Celery tasks and management commands run without tenant context. Examples are the OTP cleanup task, sync_permissions_roles, load_govt_organization_csv and load_fixtures. They will hit only the public schema unless wrapped (e.g. tenant-schemas-celery, tenant_command or all_tenants_command).
Keycloak becomes a second identity store. CARE's User keeps a local password, totp_secret and mfa_settings, which duplicates Keycloak's job and risks MFA bypass if the local login stays enabled.
MobileOTP scope decides patient-login isolation. If it is shared, an OTP or session issued on one hospital's subdomain could be accepted on another. Keep it per tenant and bind tokens to the tenant.

Integer-array and JSON soft references (parent_cache, geo_organization_cache, internal_organization_cache, organization_cache, users_cache, managing_organizations, facility_identifiers keyed by facility id, RoleAssociation.context_id) are not FK-enforced. They break silently if a hospital's data is moved, merged or copied between schemas (onboarding imports, tenant split or merge) without remapping IDs. If Organization is shared, organization_cache will hold public-schema IDs inside tenant rows.

'Instance' scope in CARE (SlugBaseModel 'i-' slugs, PatientIdentifierConfig with facility NULL, Patient.instance_identifiers and instance_tags, Facility.is_public) assumes one deployment is one organisation. Under schema-per-tenant these silently become per-tenant for tenant tables but stay global for any table kept in public. Every 'instance' feature needs to be checked against the scope chosen for its table.

Upstream bug: Patient.rebuild_organization_cache adds patient_organization.id (the PatientOrganization PK) to organization_cache instead of patient_organization.organization.id. Organization-based patient access checks may compare the wrong IDs. This is not caused by tenancy but affects the authorization the tenancy layer relies on. Report it upstream rather than patching it locally.

external_id UUIDs are unique per schema only. Any public-level lookup by external_id (for example a cross-tenant index, or Keycloak claims carrying a CARE external_id) must also record the tenant. uuid4 makes real collisions negligible.

The AbstractUser M2Ms to auth.Group and auth.Permission and the contenttypes framework must stay in SHARED_APPS alongside users.User. If they are also in TENANT_APPS, the duplicated contenttypes IDs need care for any generic relations.
RoleAssociation appears to be dead code: it has a generic context/context_id soft reference and no references outside its definition. If it is revived, context_id integer IDs are schema-local.

django-tenants splits tables by Django APP, not by model. Every model reviewed here, plus Patient, Organization, ValueSet, ProductKnowledge and TagConfig, is in the single 'emr' app. Any 'shared' or 'either' choice for an emr model therefore cannot be expressed through SHARED_APPS/TENANT_APPS alone. Putting emr in both lists creates every emr table in public AND in every tenant schema. Unqualified FK REFERENCES then resolve through search_path to the tenant's own copy, so a 'shared' row in public is never the FK target. A per-model split needs a custom DB router (allow_migrate per model), moving models into a new app (an upstream edit), or keeping all of emr tenant and seeding reference rows per tenant.
model_risks.evidence: apps/backend/care/emr/apps.py:5-7 (single EMRConfig name='care.emr'); all models in the scope files use app label 'emr'

model_risks.risk: The global login wants users.User shared (public), but User has FKs into tenant models: home_facility to facility.Facility, and geo_organization to emr.Organization (tenant, if emr is tenant). The public schema migration would reference tables that do not exist there, and a shared row cannot point at a per-tenant row. This is a shared-to-tenant FK that Postgres cannot express under django-tenants. It needs a minimal logged edit (e.g. drop the FK or replace it with a soft ref, or move home facility into a per-tenant membership table).
model_risks.evidence: apps/backend/care/users/models.py:117-119 (geo_organization FK emr.Organization), apps/backend/care/users/models.py:142-144 (home_facility FK facility.Facility PROTECT)

model_risks.risk: Tenant tables FK into the shared users.User with on_delete=CASCADE or PROTECT. Django's deletion collector only sees the current schema. Deleting or merging a User from public either fails at commit on a deferred FK from another tenant's schema, or (run inside a tenant) hard-deletes clinical rows in that tenant only. CASCADE on clinical data also conflicts with retention (NABH/DPDP). User lifecycle must be handled as deactivate-only, never delete, with per-tenant reassignment.
model_risks.evidence: apps/backend/care/emr/models/observation.py:17-24 (data_entered_by CASCADE); service_request.py:39-45 (requester CASCADE); medication_request.py:14-16 (prescribed_by CASCADE); file_upload.py:25-31 and report/report_upload.py:26-32 (archived_by PROTECT); favorites.py:19 (user CASCADE); base.py:11-26 (created_by/updated_by SET_NULL on every model)

model_risks.risk: The Redis favourites cache has no tenant namespace. Keys use the per-schema integer facility.id (likely 1 in many tenants) and user.id. A doctor who works at two hospitals gets lists that collide or overwrite each other, which leaks the other hospital's favourite list names and resource ids into the wrong tenant. The facility=None key ('-') is fully shared. CACHES sets no tenant-aware KEY_FUNCTION (e.g. django_tenants.cache.make_key) or KEY_PREFIX in base settings.

Object storage is not partitioned by tenant. FileUpload and ReportUpload use a class-level S3FilesManager per BucketType, and object keys are '{file_type}/{internal_name}' in one bucket per type. All hospitals' PHI files share one keyspace and bucket policy. Per-tenant export, DPDP erasure, retention and CERT-In scoping, and blast-radius limits all need a tenant prefix or per-tenant bucket. That is an edit to care/emr/utils/file_manager.py or a plugin override.

Instance-wide definitions (facility NULL, 'i-' slugs) assume ONE shared catalogue visible to every facility. Only is_superuser can create or edit them, and list endpoints merge facility rows with facility__isnull rows. Under schema-per-tenant these become per-tenant copies, so a platform master catalogue needs a seed or sync job for every tenant (hundreds of schemas) plus migration of updates. Alternatively they are made shared, but their facility FK into the tenant facility.Facility (and inbound CASCADE/PROTECT FKs from tenant clinical rows) blocks that without a split model.

Global is_superuser on a shared User grants platform-wide powers in every tenant: creating instance-level definitions and templates, and editing or deleting any questionnaire. In SaaS, the hospital-admin role and the platform-operator role must be separated (Keycloak org roles). Otherwise a superuser flag set for one hospital applies in all of them.

Questionnaire is instance-global upstream (no facility FK, globally unique slug), but it stores per-hospital access in internal_organization_cache (FacilityOrganization ids) and links to FacilityOrganization. It cannot be one shared row per form. As a tenant model, the standard CARE and system forms must be seeded into each tenant, slug uniqueness becomes per-schema, and render_responses() always uses the current definition, so a later platform-wide form update changes how past responses render in every tenant that receives it.

Many integer-PK ArrayField soft references have no FK integrity and are meaningful only within one schema. Any tenant cloning, seeding from a template tenant, moving a facility between tenants or cross-tenant analytics must remap them. If a referenced model (TagConfig, Organization, definitions) ends up shared while the referrer is tenant, id spaces mix silently.
model_risks.evidence: encounter.py:24,27,35; service_request.py:20,46; activity_definition.py:20-24,33; questionnaire.py:19-20,155-156; medication_request.py:20; medication_dispense.py:45; favorites.py:20; allergy_intolerance.py:18-20

model_risks.risk: Model save() side-effects and EMR signals must run in the right schema. Encounter.save() calls sync_organization_cache (a second save that reads facility.default_internal_organization_id). EncounterOrganization, QuestionnaireOrganization and QuestionnaireFacilityOrganization saves rewrite parent caches. care.emr.signals is wired in AppConfig.ready. Celery tasks or management commands that touch these models need tenant context (e.g. tenant-schemas-celery / schema_context), or they write into public or the wrong tenant.

Slug uniqueness for SlugBaseModel definitions is enforced only in viewset code (no DB constraint), with an exists() check that is race-prone. The calculated facility slug embeds the facility external_id ('f-<uuid>-slug'). This is safe per tenant, but any shared or master-catalogue sync has to reproduce the 'i-' slug convention exactly, or lookups by slug (ActivityDefinition requirements, questionnaire response templates) break.

Generic UUID or string soft references (Observation.subject_id/parent, QuestionnaireResponse.subject_id, FileUpload/ReportUpload.associating_id, MetaArtifact.associating_external_id) are resolved by external_id lookups in the current schema. Under schema isolation this is safe: a foreign tenant's UUID just returns 404. But there is no DB integrity, and code that runs without tenant context (public schema) silently resolves nothing. BaseModel.external_id unique=True becomes per-schema unique, so an external_id alone no longer identifies the tenant, and every API or deep link must carry the tenant (subdomain).

If ProductKnowledge (which also has instance-wide facility-NULL rows) were made shared, the tenant clinical FKs into it (MedicationAdministration.administered_product with on_delete=CASCADE) would mean deleting one shared product cascades, or is blocked, across hundreds of tenant schemas. Django cannot collect that, and the DB FK would fail at commit.

Cache keys built from integer PKs collide across tenants. In schema-per-tenant every schema has its own id sequences, so facility_id=1 exists in every tenant. Tenant B could read Tenant A's discount and monetary configuration, which would put wrong prices or discounts on invoices.
model_risks.evidence: care/emr/models/facility_config.py:33-39 (key 'facility:{facility_id}:...'), :50-57 and :62-72 (cache.get/set), :76-77 (cache.delete). Fix: a django-tenants tenant-aware cache KEY_FUNCTION (django_tenants.cache.make_key) in settings. No model edit is needed.

model_risks.risk: Celery tasks take bare integer ids and have no tenant context. A worker runs in the public schema (or whatever search_path it last had), so it gets DoesNotExist or silently updates another tenant's row with the same id. Every .delay() call across CARE needs tenant propagation (e.g. tenant-schemas-celery).
model_risks.evidence: care/emr/models/resource_category.py:123-140 (summarise_monetary_components @shared_task, .delay(component.id) at :140; also called at api/viewsets/resource_category.py:208). care/emr/models/location.py:160-168 (handle_cascade @app.task, currently invoked synchronously at :129 and :168).

model_risks.risk: ResourceRequest is an inter-facility workflow. Its origin, approving and assigned facilities are different hospitals, so different tenants. Postgres/django-tenants cannot hold FKs across tenant schemas, and the comments thread is written by the other hospital's staff. Under schema-per-tenant this needs a redesign, for example a public-schema exchange or referral record with UUID soft references and tenant ids, or it must be disabled.

Several models mix scopes: a NULL facility means an instance-wide row shared by all facilities. These look like shared data, but they cannot move to the public schema, because a shared table cannot have FKs into tenant tables (ResourceCategory, FacilityOrganization, Facility). The workable option is to keep them in the tenant schema and seed or sync the instance-wide rows into every tenant. That needs a sync command run on each tenant's creation and on each upstream sync.
model_risks.evidence: ProductKnowledge: product_knowledge.py:7-9 (nullable facility), :21-26 (FK to the facility-bound ResourceCategory), viewset api/viewsets/inventory/product_knowledge.py:176,193. TagConfig: tag_config.py:15-33 (nullable facility, FK to FacilityOrganization and Organization), tagging/base.py:46,118, api/viewsets/tag_config.py:101-104. HealthcareService: healthcare_service.py:8-14.

model_risks.risk: Integer soft references in ArrayFields have no DB constraint. They hold TagConfig ids (tags), FacilityOrganization ids (facility_organization_cache), FacilityLocation ids (HealthcareService.locations), ChargeItem ids (Invoice.charge_items) and parent_cache ids. If any referenced model is split across public and tenant schemas, or data is migrated between schemas (onboarding an existing CARE install, merging or splitting tenants), these ids silently point at the wrong rows. The referenced models must stay tenant-local, and migration tooling must remap the arrays.
model_risks.evidence: account.py:28; charge_item.py:48; charge_item_definition.py:20; invoice.py:25; supply_request.py:26; supply_delivery.py:43; location.py:22,29,39; device.py:38; healthcare_service.py:21; tag_config.py:40; resource_category.py:30; scheduling/booking.py:36.

model_risks.risk: users.User is shared (global Keycloak login), but every tenant table has FKs to it. Some use CASCADE. Django's deletion collector only sees the current schema, so hard-deleting a User would either fail on the FK constraints in other schemas at commit, or cascade-delete billing and appointment rows in only one tenant. Users must never be hard-deleted; deactivate them instead. CASCADE on performer_actor could wipe charge items.
model_risks.evidence: base.py:11-26 (created_by/updated_by on every model); charge_item.py:49-55 (performer_actor CASCADE); scheduling/booking.py:33 (booked_by CASCADE); scheduling/schedule.py:11-13 (SchedulableResource.user CASCADE); resource_request.py:40-45; valueset.py:60 (UserValueSetPreference.user CASCADE).

model_risks.risk: ValueSet.slug is globally unique, and slugs are soft-referenced from questionnaires and evaluators. Shared: one copy is kept and hospital-authored sets need a namespace prefix, but a hospital's custom set would be visible to all tenants unless filtered. Tenant: the unique constraint is per schema, and sync_valueset or the registry must run in every schema after each upstream sync. ValueSet.search/lookup call the terminology server, so all tenants share that dependency (see P1-T10).

Recent and favourite code keys bypass the Django cache key function. RecentViewsManager uses a raw django_redis connection with a class-level cached client, and keys have no tenant prefix. A django-tenants KEY_FUNCTION will NOT cover them. A doctor at two hospitals shares recents across tenants, which could leak hospital-specific codes if value sets are tenant-local with the same slug.

emr.Organization is the FK target for suppliers and some tags. It mixes globally shared 'govt' (geographic) organizations with hospital-specific 'product_supplier', 'team' and 'role' organizations. If Organization is made shared to keep the govt hierarchy as one copy, each hospital's supplier list lands in the public schema and is visible to every tenant. It probably needs to be split, or kept as tenant with the govt rows seeded.
model_risks.evidence: care/emr/models/supply_request.py:27-32 and supply_delivery.py:44-46 (supplier -> emr.Organization); tag_config.py:28-33; resources/organization/spec.py:10-14 (OrganizationTypeChoices team/govt/role/product_supplier).

model_risks.risk: Almost every model has a non-null FK to facility.Facility, and model code relies on Facility's tenant-side relations (default_internal_organization, the root FacilityOrganization). Facility must therefore stay in the tenant schema. Routing, i.e. subdomain to schema, needs a separate public Tenant/Domain model; Facility must not be moved to public.
model_risks.evidence: location.py:23 and :99 (self.facility.default_internal_organization_id); device.py:43-45 (root FacilityOrganization lookup by facility); facility FKs in account.py:8, charge_item.py:8, invoice.py:8, scheduling/token.py:12,28,42,56, etc.

model_risks.risk: Integer PKs and per-facility counters are only unique within a schema. That is correct inside a tenant. Anything that leaves the schema (accounting outbox to Tally/ERPNext, analytics, audit logs, Celery payloads, ABDM callbacks) must key on (tenant, external_id UUID), never on the integer id. Invoice number, built from invoice_number_expression, is not DB-unique even within a tenant.
model_risks.evidence: care/utils/models/base.py:16 (external_id UUID unique); invoice.py:31 (number, no constraint); facility_config.py:14-16 (invoice_number_expression); scheduling/token.py:77-86 (Token.get_next_number MAX+1, no unique constraint).

model_risks.risk: SlugBaseModel's 'i-' instance-scoped slugs assume one instance-wide namespace. Under schema-per-tenant, 'i-' becomes per tenant, so the same 'i-' slug can mean different definitions in different hospitals. Slug uniqueness is not enforced in the DB even within a tenant (index only).
model_risks.evidence: care/emr/models/base.py:32-64 (calculate_slug / parse_slug); resource_category.py:48-51 (Index slug+facility, not unique); api/viewsets/inventory/product_knowledge.py:82-88.

model_risks.risk: FacilityMonetoryConfig.get_monetory_config lazily INSERTs a row whenever none exists. If it is called without tenant context (Celery, a management command, the public schema), it will create rows in the wrong schema or fail on the FK.

Schedule.is_public implies anonymous or public booking endpoints. These must resolve the tenant from the subdomain before any query, otherwise they hit the public schema. A doctor working at two hospitals has independent SchedulableResource, Schedule and AvailabilityException rows per tenant, so leave or double-booking across hospitals is not detected.
model_risks.evidence: care/emr/models/scheduling/schedule.py:58 (is_public), :6-35 (SchedulableResource unique per facility+user), :72-79 (AvailabilityException per resource).
